title: Finding and counting equipment across two craft rooms
beneficiary: Volunteer workshop stewards and participants using shared equipment in two community craft rooms.
valued_outcome: People can find an available item of the requested type, and the steward can reconcile the inventory without interrupting an ongoing workshop.
success_measure: During four weekly sessions, at least 90% of equipment requests are fulfilled within two minutes; the closing count differs from the verified physical count by no more than one item.

hard_constraints_with_source.text: All 48 currently owned items must retain their existing permanent asset numbers, which appear in the donation register.
Changes may use at most 60 currency units of materials and two hours of initial steward time.
Ordinary participants must be able to borrow equipment without providing a personal phone, account, or contact information.
Both rooms must remain available for their scheduled workshops; equipment storage must fit within the existing four cabinets.

changeable_assumptions: Cabinet assignments were inherited from the previous steward and have no contractual status.
A single paper list currently serves both as the donation inventory and as the record of where items belong.
incumbent_description: Each item has a small numbered sticker. Cabinet doors carry handwritten type names. Participants take items themselves, while a steward marks returns on a paper sheet after each session.

supplied_observations.text: The inventory contains 20 handheld magnifiers, 16 desk timers, and 12 tabletop whiteboards; all 48 were physically present last Friday.
Across 30 timed requests, 22 were fulfilled within two minutes, five took between two and five minutes, and three were abandoned.
Seven items had stickers that could be read only by turning the item over; three cabinet headings used abbreviations unfamiliar to new volunteers.
The previous four closing counts differed from the following morning’s physical counts by zero, three, two, and one items respectively.
Equipment moved between rooms during six of eight observed sessions. Twelve participants and two volunteers normally attend each session.
A complete closing count currently takes 14 minutes. Stewards recorded no missing equipment or requests for additional item types during the observation period.

unmeasured_variables: How much search time occurs at cabinets versus at occupied tables.
Whether workshop size or volunteer experience affects the recorded counting discrepancies.
available_resources: One willing steward, blank removable labels, ordinary stationery, and a printer available between sessions.
Access to all equipment before the next four weekly workshops.
evidence_provenance: authored synthetic case; observations stipulated not real empirical data
